variables.label: Baseline yearly risk α_t
variables.fields: the outcome itself (who tipped which year)
steps: One intercept per year 2012–15, fit by the model (year dummies).
It is the log-odds of tipping that year for a tract with every other input at the at-risk average.
The test years 2016–17 were never seen, so they get the average of the 2012–15 intercepts.

variables.label: Starting income
steps: ACS 2006–10 median household income for the tract.
Natural log (a $10k gap matters more at $25k than at $90k).

variables.label: Starting rent
steps: ACS 2006–10 median gross rent.
Natural log.

variables.label: Starting college share
steps: Add up the men and women 25+ with a bachelor's, master's, professional or doctorate.
Divide by all adults 25+. Percent.

variables.label: Starting renter share
steps: Renter-occupied households ÷ all occupied households. Percent.

variables.label: Own rent change so far
steps: Rent growth since 2010: rent(t−1) ÷ rent(2010) − 1.
Rank it against all 2,000+ NYC tracts that year: 0 = slowest, 1 = fastest.

variables.label: Own college-share change so far
steps: College share(t−1) − college share(2010), in points.
Rank against all NYC tracts that year (0–1).

variables.label: Renovation permits
variables.fields: job_type = A1, permit_type = AL, filing_status = INITIAL
steps: Count distinct permit jobs issued in the tract that year (each job counted once).
Divide by the tract's 2006–10 households, × 1,000.
log(1 + rate) so a few busy tracts don't dominate.

variables.label: New-building permits
variables.fields: job_type = NB, permit_type = NB, filing_status = INITIAL
steps: Count distinct new-building jobs issued that year.
Per 1,000 households, then log(1 + rate).

variables.label: Demolition permits
variables.fields: job_type = DM, permit_type = DM, filing_status = INITIAL
steps: Count distinct full-demolition jobs issued that year.
Per 1,000 households, then log(1 + rate).

variables.label: Home sales
steps: Keep residential sales ≥ $10,000 (drops $0 family transfers).
Place each sale in a tract by its tax lot (PLUTO), or its block if the lot is new.
Count per 1,000 households, then log(1 + rate).

variables.label: Home price growth
variables.fields: sale price ÷ residential units, 1–3 family homes
steps: Price per unit for every 1–3 family sale ≥ $10,000.
Median over the two years ending t−1, and over 2009–10 (the base).
Growth = log(median now ÷ median base). Needs 5+ sales in each; otherwise uses the neighborhood (NTA).

variables.label: Felony change
steps: Place each felony complaint in a tract by its coordinates.
Felonies per 1,000 residents in t−1 and in 2009.
Change = log((rate t−1 + 1) ÷ (rate 2009 + 1)). Negative = crime fell.

variables.label: Noise complaints
steps: Place each noise complaint in a tract by its coordinates.
Complaints per 1,000 residents.
Relative to the city that year: log((tract + 1) ÷ (city + 1)). 311 use grew citywide, this removes that.

variables.label: Subway distance
steps: Distance in km from the tract's center to the nearest subway (or SIR) station.
Fixed over time: almost no stations opened 2010–17.

variables.label: Neighbors' rent change
variables.fields: own rent-change rank of each touching tract
steps: Neighbors = tracts that share a border or corner (queen contiguity).
Average their rent-change ranks (t−1).

variables.label: Neighbors' college change
variables.fields: own college-change rank of each touching tract
steps: Average the neighbors' college-change ranks (t−1).

variables.label: Affluent edge next door
variables.fields: which neighbors were not low-income in 2006–10
steps: Share of neighbors that were never at risk (not in the bottom 40% of income).

variables.label: Neighbors' renovation permits
steps: Average the neighbors' renovation permits value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Neighbors' new-building permits
steps: Average the neighbors' new-building permits value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Neighbors' demolition permits
steps: Average the neighbors' demolition permits value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Neighbors' home sales
steps: Average the neighbors' home sales value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Neighbors' home price growth
steps: Average the neighbors' home price growth value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Neighbors' felony change
steps: Average the neighbors' felony change value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Neighbors' noise complaints
steps: Average the neighbors' noise complaints value (same units as the tract's own).

variables.label: Place effect u_i
steps: One number per tract: how much more (or less) likely it tips than its inputs say.
The ICAR prior pulls each tract's u toward its neighbors' average, with strength τ (picked by cross-validation).
Captures what we didn't measure but is shared locally (a new park, a school, a reputation).
